title: audit.jsonl row
description: One line of MOLTBOOK_HOME/logs/audit.jsonl, the approval gate's record (ADR-0012). The writer is cli/approval.py::_log_decision (single owner of the row shape); append_jsonl_restricted stamps run_id / session_id. The key for joining a row to anything else is content_hash (sha256 of the text handed to the logger, first 16 hex). path is a reference only: it is MOLTBOOK_HOME-relative when the target is inside the home (absolute otherwise), and 'rows before 2026-10-24 carry an absolute path'. Rows are append-only; older rows lack keys listed in x-writer-keys and are valid (see x-since). The integrity model is in docs/adr/0012-human-approval-gate.md (2026-10-24 addendum): append-only, mode 0600, the prev hash chain is the tamper-evidence surface, content_hash is an identifier and not a signature.

ts.description: UTC ISO-8601, seconds precision. Pre-2026-04 rows use 'timestamp' instead; readers accept both.

command.description: CLI subcommand that produced the artifact (insight, distill-identity, amend-constitution, remove-skill, adopt-staged, correction, ...).

path.description: Target path, MOLTBOOK_HOME-relative when inside the home (x-since 2026-10-24; earlier rows are absolute). For a remove-skill / archive row, the file the row is about. Reference only; the key is content_hash.

decision.description: staged: written to .staged/, decision deferred. approved / rejected: the gate's verdict. validation_failed: a generation that failed validation and never reached the gate (amend-constitution, P0-04.5; reason says why). corrected: a hand-appended correction row (command=correction). held: historical only (adopt-staged --hold-names, 2026-08-15..2026-09-19, removed by RFC-0042 item 5); readers must keep tolerating it.

source.description: Which path reached the gate; mirrors cli/approval.py::AuditSource (a test pins the two together). A planned 'takedown' value (P3-05.14) is not in the enum until the writer has it.

content_hash.description: sha256(text)[:16]. The join key between a stage row, its adopt / reject row, a .rejected/<ts>-<content_hash>.md file and a gate_item. For adopt rows the text is the canonicalized body BEFORE the trailing newline.

snapshot_path.description: Pivot snapshot directory of the run that generated the candidate, MOLTBOOK_HOME-relative (ADR-0020). Non-null for new stage and stage-* rows whose producer took a snapshot (P1-12.9).

reason.description: The human's reason, free text. Required by the CLI for remove-skill, adopt-staged --yes and names-file rejections (via reason_code).

reason_code.description: Why a candidate was rejected; null on rows that are not rejections or whose gate predates the field.

channel.description: The door the decision came through. tty: a prompt was shown to a terminal. names-file: transcribed from --adopt-names / --reject-names / --archive-names FILE. yes-flag: --yes. headless: no terminal and no human at the keyboard (stage rows, a piped prompt).

session.description: The session the decision was taken in (Claude Code session id, or a weekly run_id). Names the transcriber; approver names the human.

approver.description: The human who decided (D-P1-12-2 = B): the '# approver:' signature line of the names FILE, --approver, or MOLTBOOK_OPERATOR. Null when nothing said; never a constant filled in by code. Registered names: docs/GOVERNANCE.md (Accountable operator).

source_ids.description: Lineage keys of the artifact's inputs (ADR-0050).

epistemic_counts.description: Provenance-kind tally of the input patterns (ADR-0050 / ADR-0082).

prev.description: sha256(raw previous line)[:16]; null for the first row; 'unreadable' when the writer could not read its predecessor. Absent before 2026-10-09 (legacy rows).

run_id.description: Process run id stamped by append_jsonl_restricted (ADR-0078).

session_id.description: Agent-session id, stamped only while a 'run' session is active.

corrects_ts.description: correction rows: ts of the row being corrected.

mv_from.description: correction rows: MOLTBOOK_HOME-relative path the file was hand-moved from (the path the corrected row recorded).

mv_to.description: correction rows: path it was moved to (equals this row's path).

sha_checked.description: correction rows: the sha256[:16] of the live file, verified equal to the corrected row's content_hash.

x-join.adoption_to_stage: a stage-adopted* / stage-rejected-names row's content_hash equals the content_hash of the earlier stage row of the same command (the adopt hash is taken after canonicalization, so a candidate whose frontmatter name was normalized at write time joins by command + snapshot_path + ts order instead).
x-join.stage_to_snapshot: snapshot_path names the producer's snapshot directory directly when non-null; otherwise the stage row's run_id equals that snapshot's manifest.json run_id.
x-join.legacy_fallback: 18 manifests written before run_id was stamped, and rows before 2026-10-24 without snapshot_path, resolve by ts neighbourhood (same command, within one minute) and are marked 'inferred' by the resolver, never exact.
x-join.gate_item_to_audit: a gate_item event's content_hash equals the content_hash of exactly one approved / rejected row (scripts/gate_item_audit_join.py).

x-correction-row: A hand-appended row with command='correction', decision='corrected', source='correction' records an out-of-band repair of an earlier row's path (who: approver; when: ts; what: mv_from -> mv_to; evidence: sha_checked). It does not replace the corrected row; readers join them by content_hash.
